subject: series
synopsis: Selina Kyle's 1993-2001 solo series, defined by Jim Balent's long art run and Jo Duffy and Doug Moench's scripts, through Devin Grayson's Gotham tenure.
author: Devin Grayson, Jim Balent

subject: series
synopsis: The Kree warrior Mar-Vell's original series (1968-1979), revitalized by Jim Starlin's cosmic Thanos saga in #25-34.

subject: series
synopsis: Wildstorm's runaway super-teens Fairchild, Grunge, Freefall, Burnout and Rainmaker on the run from Team 7 and I.O., later written by Adam Warren and John Arcudi.

subject: series
synopsis: Gold Key/Dell's solo Bugs Bunny comics. The character's wit and confidence translate surprisingly well to print in the best issues.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Yuto Suzuki's action comedy about a retired legendary hitman trying to live peacefully as a convenience store owner while being constantly dragged back. Inventive action choreography and warm family dynamics.
author: Yuto Suzuki

subject: series
synopsis: Dan Jurgens's Heroes Return Thor (1998-2004): Thor bonds with EMT Jake Olson, then rules Asgard and Earth in The Reigning.

subject: series
synopsis: Roy Thomas's 1981-1987 series gathering DC's Golden Age heroes on Earth-Two into a wartime super-team after Pearl Harbor, steeped in continuity and history.
author: Roy Thomas, Dann Thomas

subject: series
synopsis: Larry Hama's original G.I. Joe continuity, carried from Marvel and IDW to Skybound/Image, continuing the classic numbering from #301 in the Energon Universe.

subject: series
synopsis: Atrocitus and the rage-fueled Red Lantern Corps in their New 52 series, later led by Guy Gardner under Charles Soule.

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's romance-focused digital anthology. Touching character studies exploring relationships across the Marvel universe in the digital scroll format.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: IDW and DC comics based on Craig McCracken's cartoon. Captures the show's bright energy and action-comedy balance well.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Namor's first solo series (1968-1974), spun out of Tales to Astonish: Roy Thomas and John Buscema, later Bill Everett's return to his creation.

subject: series
synopsis: Joshua Williamson's 2023 Superman: a reformed, imprisoned Lex Luthor's company becomes Superman's, while the Super-family faces new Metropolis threats.
author: Joshua Williamson

subject: series
synopsis: Jolyne Cujoh, Jotaro's daughter, is framed and jailed in a Florida prison, where she battles Stand users serving Dio's disciple Enrico Pucci.

subject: series
synopsis: Al Ewing and Ram V's 2021 Venom: Eddie Brock becomes the symbiote god across time while his son Dylan takes up the Venom mantle.
author: Ram V

subject: series
synopsis: Jim Valentino's 1990 revival of the original 31st-century Guardians of the Galaxy — Vance Astro, Starhawk, Yondu and Martinex — searching for Captain America's shield.

subject: series
synopsis: Gold Key's Road Runner and Wile E. Coyote comics. Translates the pursuit-and-fail cartoon formula to print with variable success.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Gold Key's 1969-1976 adaptation of the gothic soap opera, with vampire Barnabas Collins at Collinwood, drawn largely by Joe Certa.

subject: series
synopsis: Guy Gardner's solo series, where he discovers alien heritage and replaces his ring with shapeshifting weaponry. Better than expected — Beau Smith's run has genuine bravado humor.
author: Beau Smith

subject: series
synopsis: Zeb Wells's 2009 reunion of the original New Mutants as adults, later continued by Abnett and Lanning, through Second Coming and Fear Itself.
author: Zeb Wells

subject: series
synopsis: Comics criticism and analysis magazine. Thoughtful essays on comics as a medium from a contemporary perspective.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Various takes on Batman's team of outside-the-law heroes. The Judd Winick run on the 2000s series is the best — morally complex superhero action with genuine emotional stakes.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Hiro Mashima's space adventure manga — a spiritual successor to Fairy Tail with a more sci-fi setting. Same core themes of friendship and found family, in a more ambitious world.
author: Hiro Mashima

subject: series
synopsis: Stephen Hillenburg's own bimonthly SpongeBob anthology from United Plankton, mixing house stories with guest cartoonists.

subject: series
synopsis: Charles Soule's 2020 Marvel Star Wars, following Luke, Leia, Han and the Rebellion regrouping after The Empire Strikes Back.
author: Charles Soule

subject: series
synopsis: Scott Snyder and Greg Capullo's New 52 Batman (2011-2016): the Court of Owls, Death of the Family, Zero Year and Endgame.
author: Scott Snyder

subject: series
synopsis: Bat-family focused series (2000-2006) about Batman's relationships with Nightwing, Robin, Oracle and Alfred, with Batman Black and White backups.

subject: series
synopsis: A Garfield collection exploring the cat's adventures and humor.

subject: series
synopsis: Al Ewing's acclaimed current run reframing Thor as myth and legend rather than superhero. Deeply literary, drawing on Norse mythology with genuine craft. Some of the best Thor material since Simonson.
author: Al Ewing

subject: series
synopsis: Moon Knight's 90s volume, written partly by J.M. DeMatteis. Stronger than its reputation — the early DeMatteis issues are psychologically rich explorations of Marc Spector's dissociation.
author: J.M. DeMatteis

subject: series
synopsis: Cody Ziglar's 2022 Miles Morales series, following Miles through Trial by Spider and Bad Blood as Brooklyn's Spider-Man.

subject: series
synopsis: Jed MacKay and C.F. Villa's 2023 Avengers: Captain Marvel leads a new core team against multiversal threats like the Twilight Court.

subject: series
synopsis: Valiant's 1991-1996 revival of Gold Key's 41st-century robot-smashing hero in North Am, a cornerstone of the early Valiant universe.

subject: series
synopsis: Tite Kubo's shinigami epic. The Soul Society arc is exceptional shonen manga; later arcs become increasingly convoluted but the core concept and character designs remain among the best in the genre.
author: Tite Kubo

subject: series
synopsis: Fabian Nicieza's fan-favourite ongoing series pairing the idealistic messiah Cable with the anarchic mercenary Deadpool in an unlikely buddy-comedy partnership that doubles as sharp political satire.
author: Fabian Nicieza

subject: series
synopsis: The original French science fiction and fantasy comics anthology founded by Jean Giraud (Moebius), Philippe Druillet, and Jean-Pierre Dionnet; one of the most artistically important comics magazines ever published.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Carl Potts and Jim Lee's 1988 companion Punisher series, followed by Chuck Dixon's vigilante war stories.
author: Chuck Dixon, Mike Baron

subject: series
synopsis: Archie's long-running Sonic tie-in comics. Developed a surprisingly elaborate mythology and original characters far beyond the games. Passionate fanbase; the Ian Flynn era particularly strong.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Vertigo's ongoing about Tim Hunter, a London teen destined to be the greatest magician of his age; John Ney Rieber wrote #1-50, Peter Gross the rest.

subject: series
synopsis: DC's ambitious weekly series set in the year following Infinite Crisis, with no Superman, Batman, or Wonder Woman. Geoff Johns, Grant Morrison, Greg Rucka, and Mark Waid writing together produced a surprisingly cohesive and satisfying epic.
author: Mark Waid, Geoff Johns, Grant Morrison, Greg Rucka

subject: series
synopsis: James Robinson and David Goyer's revived Justice Society emphasized legacy and history in ways uniquely possible with DC's oldest characters. Geoff Johns's long subsequent run is warm-hearted, well-crafted superhero comics.
author: James Robinson, David Goyer

subject: series
synopsis: Homura Kawamoto's high-stakes gambling manga set in a school where social status is determined by gambling. Psychologically intense with an extraordinary protagonist — Yumeko Jabami is one of manga's most compelling leads.
author: Homura Kawamoto

subject: series
synopsis: Tadashi Agi and Shu Okimoto's wine manga — genuinely educational and dramatically compelling. An unusual masterwork.
author: Tadashi Agi

subject: series
synopsis: Daniel Way's exploration of Wolverine's forgotten past. Connects the dots of the character's history methodically; the introduction of Daken as Wolverine's son is genuinely interesting. The plotting can be laborious.
author: Daniel Way

subject: series
synopsis: Alan Grant's 1993-1999 ongoing for the Main Man, DC's ultra-violent space bounty hunter, in gonzo satirical adventures.
author: Alan Grant

subject: series
synopsis: Gerry Duggan and Brian Posehn's 2012 Deadpool: zombie presidents, the Good, the Bad and the Ugly, Wade's marriage and Axis.
author: Brian Posehn, Daniel Way

subject: series
synopsis: The adjectiveless 1990 Spider-Man launched by Todd McFarlane's record-breaking #1, continuing through the Clone Saga and Howard Mackie's tenure.
author: Howard Mackie

subject: series
synopsis: Digital anthology exploring various corners of the Avengers mythology. Accessible one-shots.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Vita Ayala's run on New Mutants during the Krakoa Era focuses on the younger generation of mutants adjusting to life on the island nation, exploring themes of trauma, recovery, and belonging with a particularly empathetic voice. A character-driven complement to the larger X-Men line.
author: Vita Ayala

subject: series
synopsis: Part of Alan Moore's celebrated run on Supreme, reimagining the Superman-analogue with Silver Age sensibility and clever meta-commentary.
author: Alan Moore

subject: series
synopsis: Kosuke Fujishima's motorcycle racing manga. High-energy racing sequences with a charming protagonist learning from a legendary female rider.
author: Kosuke Fujishima

subject: series
synopsis: Hiro Mashima's fantasy shonen about Natsu, Lucy and the rowdy Fairy Tail wizards' guild, across 63 volumes.

subject: series
synopsis: Nakaba Suzuki's sequel series to Seven Deadly Sins, following the next generation. Familiar shonen beats executed with craft; the parent series' mythology adds depth.
author: Nakaba Suzuki

subject: series
synopsis: The New 52 Green Lantern: Geoff Johns's final arc with Sinestro wearing the ring and Hal deputized, then Robert Venditti's tenure.

subject: series
synopsis: Jack Cole's rubber-limbed crimefighter in his own Quality title (1943-1956), a Golden Age high point of slapstick, surreal visual invention and crime.
author: Jack Cole

subject: series
synopsis: Tom Taylor and Nicola Scott's 2023 Titans: Nightwing leads the former Teen Titans as the DC Universe's premier team.

subject: series
synopsis: Jed MacKay and Ryan Stegman's 2024 From the Ashes X-Men: Cyclops leads a militant team out of Alaska after Krakoa's fall.
author: Jed MacKay

subject: series
synopsis: Digital-format Avengers anthology. Light adventure stories accessible to new readers.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Fleetway's British anthology comic pitched as more grown-up than 2000 AD. Featured Grant Morrison's early work and introduced Mark Millar to UK comics. Short-lived but historically important for British comics.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Yasuhisa Hara's epic of the Warring States: war orphan Xin rises toward great general alongside Ying Zheng, the future first emperor of China.
author: Yasuhisa Hara

subject: series
synopsis: Vertigo's 1996-2001 ongoing set in Dream's realm after The Sandman, following Cain, Abel, Lucien and Matthew in rotating creators' stories.

subject: series
synopsis: Aquaman's first solo series (1962-1978): Silver Age undersea adventures with Aqualad, Mera's arrival, and the Death of a Prince saga.

subject: series
synopsis: Joshua Williamson and Simone Di Meo's 2023 Batman and Robin: Bruce and Damian try living as father and son in a new Gotham home.

subject: series
synopsis: Kelly Thompson's 2023 Birds of Prey: Black Canary assembles Cassandra Cain, Big Barda, Zealot and Harley Quinn for a rescue mission.

subject: series
synopsis: Iron Man's Heroes Return series (1998-2004): Kurt Busiek and Sean Chen's opening, then Joe Quesada and Mike Grell.

subject: series
synopsis: The New 52 Superman (2011-2016): George Pérez's launch, then Lobdell, Johns and Romita Jr.'s Men of Tomorrow and Truth.

subject: series
synopsis: Yuki Tabata's magic knight manga about a magicless boy in a world of magic users. Straightforward shonen with strong tournament arcs and improving character work. The demon-possession arc elevated the series considerably.
author: Yuki Tabata

subject: series
synopsis: Valiant's revival of the classic Gold Key character; Solar is a physicist who becomes a living god after a nuclear accident, struggling to use near-omnipotent power responsibly — Jim Shooter's plotting emphasised the human cost of such power.
author: Jim Shooter

subject: series
synopsis: Phillip Kennedy Johnson and Nic Klein's 2023 horror-road-trip Incredible Hulk: Banner and a monstrous Hulk wander America's dark folklore.

subject: series
synopsis: Daredevil volume 2 (1998-2011): Kevin Smith's Guardian Devil, Bendis and Maleev's landmark noir run, Brubaker's Hell's Kitchen, and Diggle's Shadowland.

subject: series
synopsis: Jughead Jones's 1990s-2000s solo title from Archie Comics, gag stories about food, laziness and Riverdale.

subject: series
synopsis: Howard Mackie's late 90s/early 2000s Spider-Man series. Paul Jenkins's run on the book is significantly better — particularly the short story 'The Kid Who Collects Spider-Man' reprise work.
author: Howard Mackie

subject: series
synopsis: Accessible all-ages Spider-Man. Paul Tobin's run in particular is excellent — smart, funny, and emotionally satisfying. An underrated gem for younger readers and nostalgic adults.
author: Paul Tobin

subject: series
synopsis: Gold Key's original Trek adaptations have a charmingly strange quality — drawn by artists who'd apparently never seen the show. Later DC and IDW runs are more faithful and often excellent, particularly IDW's ongoing.

subject: series
synopsis: IDW's 2018 Sonic series by Ian Flynn: Sonic and friends rebuild after Eggman's war, through the Metal Virus saga.
author: Ian Flynn, Evan Stanley

subject: series
synopsis: The New 52 Action Comics (2011-2016): Grant Morrison and Rags Morales's jeans-and-t-shirt young Superman, then Andy Diggle and Greg Pak.

subject: series
synopsis: Ed Brubaker and Steve Epting's Captain America (2004-2011): the Winter Soldier's return, the Death of Captain America, and Bucky under the shield.

subject: series
synopsis: Archie Comics' original Sabrina the Teenage Witch series (1971-1983), gentle magical humor with her aunts Hilda and Zelda and cat Salem.

subject: series
synopsis: Dan Slott's dark take on post-Civil War superhero registration — a boot camp for new heroes with sinister undertones. Underrated and surprisingly bleak.
author: Dan Slott

subject: series
synopsis: Dan Slott's 2024 series for Bailey Briggs, a Spider-Boy erased from everyone's memory, now returned and finding his place in Marvel's New York.

subject: series
synopsis: Jonathan Hickman and Marco Checchetto's 2024 Ultimate Spider-Man: a married Peter Parker with kids becomes Spider-Man late in a world remade by the Maker.

subject: series
synopsis: Daniel Warren Johnson's 2023 Skybound Transformers: the Autobots and Decepticons crash to Earth and Optimus Prime meets Spike and Carly, launching the Energon Universe.

subject: series
synopsis: Jeremy Adams's 2023 Green Lantern: Hal Jordan, stripped of the Corps after Dark Crisis, protects a quarantined Earth.

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's Vietnam War series started by Doug Murray and Michael Golden. Unusual for mainstream comics — told from the grunt's perspective with procedural accuracy and anti-war sentiment built into every arc.
author: Doug Murray

subject: series
synopsis: Gold Key's Stone Age family sitcom comics. The classic Bedrock humor formula works reliably. Mark Russell's 2016 DC revival is unexpectedly brilliant satire of modern culture.
author: Mark Russell

subject: series
synopsis: Jason Aaron's 2010 Wolverine: Logan's soul is dragged to Hell, then the Red Right Hand's revenge, back to legacy numbering #300-317.
author: Jason Aaron

subject: series
synopsis: DC's first Star Trek series (1984-1988) set during the movie era, with the Mirror Universe Saga and Mike W. Barr and Peter David scripts.

subject: series
synopsis: Cary Bates and Greg Weisman's 1987 post-Crisis Captain Atom: Air Force officer Nathaniel Adam, thrown forward in time by an alien alloy, serves as a government superhero.
author: Cary Bates, Greg Weisman

subject: series
synopsis: Brian Michael Bendis's time-travel concept of bringing the original five X-Men to the present is clever and the first volume executes it well. Lets new and legacy X-fans engage together.
author: Brian Michael Bendis

subject: series
synopsis: Alan Grant and Norm Breyfogle's 1992 Batman title exploring Arkham and Gotham's psychology, later Grant solo, Rucka and Grayson.
author: Alan Grant

subject: series
synopsis: Al Milgrom's prestige-format Marvel anthology (1982-1992), opening with Claremont and Michael Golden's Savage Land story and showcasing top artists in self-contained tales.
author: Chris Claremont, Doug Moench

subject: series
synopsis: Cody Ziglar and Rogê Antônio's 2024 relaunch of the Merc with a Mouth.

subject: series
synopsis: Janey, an undead call girl, fights demons, cults and monsters in Action Lab's Danger Zone horror-comedy.
author: Dan Mendoza

subject: series
synopsis: Tie-in to Batman: The Animated Series. Rick Burchett's clean, Timm-style art captures the show's tone exactly. Quality all-ages stories in the Animated Universe.
author: Scott Peterson

subject: series
synopsis: DC's answer to Green Lantern Corps — a space police force with less strict selection criteria. Michael Collins's run is competent sci-fi superhero work without reaching greatness.
author: Michael Jan Friedman

subject: series
synopsis: DC anthology of self-contained Justice League stories outside main continuity. Grant Morrison's opening arc 'I Can't Believe It's Not the Justice League' is excellent.
author: Grant Morrison

subject: series
synopsis: Leah Williams's 2023 Power Girl series, Karen Starr reinventing herself as a superheroine and psychic therapist in Dawn of DC.

subject: series
synopsis: Gail Simone and David Marquez's 2024 From the Ashes Uncanny X-Men: Rogue leads a team in Louisiana caring for young mutants.
author: Gail Simone

subject: series
synopsis: Kazuo Koike and Goseki Kojima's epic of Ogami Itto, the shogun's disgraced executioner, wandering Edo-period Japan as an assassin with his infant son Daigoro.

subject: series
synopsis: AC Comics' reprint series collecting golden age public domain superhero stories, part of their dedicated effort to preserve and republish classic American superhero material for modern readers.

subject: series
synopsis: DC's 80s anthology retelling hero origins. Variable quality but frequently excellent — some of the definitive takes on supporting characters and second-tier heroes appeared here.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's Ultimate Universe reimagining of the X-Men, beginning with Mark Millar and Adam Kubert's stripped-down, cinematic 'The Tomorrow People' arc and continuing through acclaimed runs by Brian Michael Bendis and others. The first arc's influence on the X-Men films was profound; the Brian Bendis era elevated the book into one of Marvel's most emotionally resonant titles.
author: Mark Millar

subject: series
synopsis: The 1960s Japanese Batman manga by Jiro Kuwata, finally collected and translated. A fascinating cultural artifact — Batman filtered through manga aesthetics, producing genuinely weird and wonderful stories.
author: Jiro Kuwata

subject: series
synopsis: Year-long weekly Batman event series with Scott Snyder and a rotating team. Ambitious scope — effectively a Batman novel — with variable execution across 52 issues.
author: Scott Snyder

subject: series
synopsis: Bongo Comics' Futurama tie-in series expanding on the world of Matt Groening's animated sci-fi comedy — Fry, Leela, Bender, and Planet Express in new adventures between episodes.
author: Ian Boothby

subject: series
synopsis: Naoshi Arakawa's women's soccer manga. Genuine character depth and tactical intelligence; a sports manga that takes its subject seriously while never losing sight of its human stories.
author: Naoshi Arakawa

subject: series
synopsis: Nunzio DeFilippis and Christina Weir's Xavier Institute students in training squads, then Kyle and Yost's darker post-M-Day run.

subject: series
synopsis: Stories from Batman's early career. Variable creative teams produce uneven results; the best issues — particularly Andy Diggle's run — are strong character studies.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Garry Trudeau's long-running political satire strip following Mike Doonesbury and friends from college through adult life; the first comic strip to win a Pulitzer Prize for Editorial Cartooning (1975).
author: Garry Trudeau

subject: series
synopsis: Jonathan Hickman's Avatar Press series imagines the gods returning to reclaim Earth from humanity. Intellectually ambitious but often gratuitously violent; the concept outpaces the execution.
author: Jonathan Hickman

subject: series
synopsis: Fred Perry's long-running independent action-comedy about an archaeologist and her were-cheetah sister. Dedicated fanbase; extremely dense mythology built over hundreds of issues.
author: Fred Perry

subject: series
synopsis: A Clark Kent in Smallville continuation from the 80s. Serviceable silver-age style storytelling that fills in Superboy's pre-Superman history.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Brian Michael Bendis's 2004 Avengers relaunch after Disassembled: Captain America, Iron Man, Spider-Man, Wolverine, Luke Cage and Spider-Woman, through Civil War, Secret Invasion and Siege.
author: Brian Michael Bendis

subject: series
synopsis: Wonder Woman's original launch anthology alongside other DC heroes. Historical golden age document; the Sensation Comics Featuring Wonder Woman digital-first revival is excellent short-form storytelling.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: DC's digital-first anthology of all-ages Wonder Woman stories by rotating creators. Consistently excellent — the format allows experimental takes on the character without continuity constraints.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Warren Ellis's Wildstorm run transformed this lackluster series into a cutting critique of superhero excess and political complicity, directly leading to The Authority. Essential reading for understanding Wildstorm.
author: Warren Ellis

subject: series
synopsis: Chris Claremont's early 2000s X-series following a team globetrotting without Xavier. Better than its reputation — Storm-focused with genuine character development.
author: Chris Claremont

subject: series
synopsis: Peter Milligan and Chris Bachalo's psychedelic Vertigo series following Rac Shade, an alien wielding the Madness Vest, traversing a surreal America. Known for Bachalo's distinctive art and Milligan's surrealist writing.
author: Peter Milligan

subject: series
synopsis: Mark Waid and Dan Mora's 2023 Shazam!: Billy Batson juggles school and heroics after his powers are rerouted through new gods.

subject: series
synopsis: The New 52 Green Lantern Corps: Guy Gardner and John Stewart lead the Corps under Peter Tomasi and Fernando Pasarin, then Van Jensen.

subject: series
synopsis: DC's 2023 anthology of Batman stories by rotating creators, headlined by Tom King and Mitch Gerads's serialized lead.

subject: series
synopsis: Peter Tomasi and Patrick Gleason's New 52 Batman and Robin (2011-2015): Bruce and Damian as father and son, from Born to Kill to Requiem and Robin Rises.

subject: series
synopsis: John Ostrander and Timothy Truman's series follows John Gaunt, a mercenary in the pan-dimensional city of Cynosure where all realities intersect; celebrated for its noir atmosphere, world-building, and morally complex protagonist.
author: John Ostrander

subject: series
synopsis: DC anthology telling definitive-era stories of iconic characters. Variable quality but excellent for character deep-dives outside main continuity.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Digital anthology visiting alternate Spider-People across the multiverse. Creative character spotlights using the vertical scroll format inventively.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: John Henry Irons in his own series following his Death of Superman introduction. Louise Simonson's run develops a compelling working-class hero with strong family ties. Underrated for the era.
author: Louise Simonson

subject: series
synopsis: Steve Orlando's 2024 Scarlet Witch, Wanda Maximoff running her magic shop and mending reality alongside her apprentice Darcy Lewis.

subject: series
synopsis: The New 52 Detective Comics (2011-2016): Tony Daniel's launch, John Layman and Jason Fabok's Emperor Penguin, then Manapul and Buccellato.
author: Tony Daniel

subject: series
synopsis: Shuichi Shigeno's legendary street racing manga follows Takumi Fujiwara, a tofu delivery boy who unknowingly becomes a genius mountain pass drifter. The definitive street racing manga that launched eurobeat memes and a passionate global fanbase.
author: Shuichi Shigeno

subject: series
synopsis: Valiant's 1992-1996 series for Gilad Anni-Padda, the immortal Fist and Steel of the Earth, mostly by John Ostrander, across eras and crossovers.

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel anthology that launched Iron Fist, Warlock, and many others. A key part of the 70s Bronze Age expansion of the Marvel line.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: X-Men volume 3 (2010-2013): Victor Gischler's Curse of the Mutants vampire launch, then Brian Wood's Storm-led security team in #30-41.

subject: series
synopsis: Rebellion's chronological reprint of every Judge Dredd story from 2000 AD, from Wagner and Ezquerra's 1977 debut onward.

subject: series
synopsis: Kurt Busiek and Mark Bagley's 2008 weekly series in which Superman, Batman and Wonder Woman are erased from the world's memory.
author: Kurt Busiek, Fabian Nicieza

subject: series
synopsis: Marc Andreyko's 2004 Manhunter: federal prosecutor Kate Spencer becomes a lethal vigilante while juggling a career and a son.
author: Marc Andreyko, John Ostrander

subject: series
synopsis: Grant Morrison's 1998 crossover set in the 853rd century. An extraordinary feat of idea-generation — a fully realized far-future DC universe sketched in detail over 36 issues.
author: Grant Morrison

subject: series
synopsis: All-ages Fantastic Four adventures. Jeff Parker's run is the standout — smart, accessible, and true to the characters' adventurous spirit.
author: Jeff Parker

subject: series
synopsis: DC's 2014 weekly set five years ahead, in a future where Brother Eye has conquered Earth and Batman Beyond travels back to stop it.

subject: series
synopsis: Hulk volume 2 (2008-2012): Jeph Loeb and Ed McGuinness's Red Hulk mystery, then Jeff Parker's well-liked Thunderbolt Ross run.

subject: series
synopsis: Los Bros Hernandez's original magazine: Jaime's Locas (Maggie and Hopey) and Gilbert's Palomar, the landmark of alternative comics.

subject: series
synopsis: The former Teen Titans as adult heroes. Devin Grayson's original run has nostalgic appeal; Tom Taylor's more recent Titans series is the current gold standard — character-rich superhero work.
author: Devin Grayson

subject: series
synopsis: Goscinny and Uderzo's Gaulish village holding out against Caesar's Rome, where Asterix and Obelix win by wit and magic potion, continued by Ferri and Conrad.
author: René Goscinny

subject: series
synopsis: Collected volumes of Dark Horse's Conan the Barbarian comics — adapting Robert E. Howard's classic sword-and-sorcery stories with faithful respect to the source material.
author: Kurt Busiek

subject: series
synopsis: Steven T. Seagle and Teddy Kristiansen's 1996 Vertigo series: a runaway shelters in a haunted house whose ghostly Juris put secret-keepers on trial.

subject: series
synopsis: Digital-first Spider-Man anthology stories. Accessible adventures for the mobile comics format.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Zot! by Scott McCloud - innovative indie superhero comic.

subject: series
synopsis: Guy Gardner's ongoing series before the Warrior relaunch. Chuck Dixon's competent superhero work with the most abrasive Green Lantern.
author: Chuck Dixon

subject: series
synopsis: Bill Willingham's long-running Vertigo series about fairy-tale characters living in exile in modern New York City after their homelands were conquered. Won numerous Eisner Awards and spawned multiple spin-offs.
author: Bill Willingham

subject: series
synopsis: Fantagraphics' archival hardcovers gathering EC Comics' 1950s horror, crime, war and SF stories artist by artist.
author: Al Feldstein, Wallace Wood

subject: series
synopsis: Joe Simon and Jack Kirby's wartime original is an extraordinary piece of American mythmaking. Captain America punching Hitler on the cover before the US entered the war was a genuine political act.
author: Joe Simon
